memory_update.text: Primary direct candidates for the food-input/menu-flexibility node are SYY, USFD, PFGC, SBUX, and TXRH.
For this node, distributors represent procurement-scale and pass-through exposure, while operators like SBUX and TXRH represent direct margin sensitivity to coffee and beef, respectively.

CMG, CAVA, WING, BROS, LKNCY, DRI, YUM, MCD, QSR, DPZ, WEN, SHAK, BLMN, DRI, CAKE, EAT, SGYA, and packaged/protein suppliers such as TSN, HRL, PPC, JBSAY, CALM, LANC, and SJM remain candidates for later passes, but were excluded here to keep the universe to five direct/obvious names.
Need a later supplier-focused pass for protein processors, coffee roasters/packaged coffee companies, dairy, packaging, and restaurant procurement/software/data vendors.

Beef and coffee are currently the clearest commodity watchpoints for this node based on USDA ERS, BLS CPI, and ICO evidence; chicken, dairy, produce, avocado, packaging, and tariffs should be tracked as secondary variables.
Add SYY and USFD as high-confidence procurement-scale and broadline foodservice distribution candidates for the food_inputs_and_menu_flexibility node.
Add TSN as the key US-listed multi-protein supplier proxy for beef/chicken substitution, cattle supply constraints, and protein cost dispersion in restaurant menus.
Add WEST as a below-$1B exception because its integrated coffee, tea, extracts, and beverage-solutions exposure is unusually direct for coffee-heavy restaurant and foodservice procurement.
Add LW as a less obvious menu-component supplier tied to high-volume QSR and foodservice frozen potato inputs, capacity decisions, and restaurant traffic sensitivity.

PFGC remains a strong follow-up candidate for broadline/specialty distribution, but was left out of the top-five limit to avoid overconcentrating this pass in distributors. Next pass should compare PFGC against SYY and USFD on customer mix, procurement efficiencies, and restaurant-chain exposure.
Add SYY, USFD, PFGC, CHEF, and WEST as public-market mappings for the restaurant food-input/procurement-flexibility node.

Broadline distributors map to procurement scale and substitution flexibility; specialty distributors map to harder-to-substitute premium center-of-plate inputs; coffee/beverage solution providers map to coffee-cost and beverage-menu repricing exposure.

Need a separate pass for protein processors, poultry/beef mix, dairy suppliers, packaging suppliers, and restaurant procurement/software vendors; TSN, HRL, PPC, LW, DAR, FRPT, MKC, INGR, and procurement-tech names require validation before inclusion.
WEST is a below-USD-1B exception and should be monitored for liquidity, leverage, customer concentration, and whether foodservice exposure is large enough to drive the equity story.

summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Expanded the Layer 1B universe around the input-cost chokepoint for restaurants. The most direct public-market mappings are broadline foodservice distributors with purchasing scale and inflation pass-through exposure, plus restaurant operators with concentrated commodity exposure. Current evidence points to beef and coffee as high-signal input categories: USDA/BLS data show food-away-from-home inflation and beef pressure remain relevant in 2026, while ICO data indicate coffee prices remain elevated versus normal historical levels. This pass intentionally limits the universe to five obvious/direct candidates and does not make investment recommendations. Layer 1B expands the restaurant input/procurement chokepoint into five US-listed candidates tied to foodservice purchasing scale, protein supply, coffee/beverage input pass-through, and high-volume menu components. The strongest direct node mappings are broadline foodservice distributors and scaled input suppliers because restaurant operators' margin resilience depends on sourcing alternatives, freight/cold-chain reliability, commodity pass-through, and menu substitution. This is research support only, not a trading recommendation. Expanded the node universe toward foodservice distributors, specialty distributors, and coffee/beverage supply-chain vendors that can benefit from or be exposed to restaurant operators' need for purchasing scale, substitution flexibility, commodity pass-through, and menu-level input management.
